text: Ahoy, {player}. Driftwood's lighthouse is still burning, if that's what you came to check.
Back on my little rock? Sit, sit. The kettle's always on.
Mind the steps. Forty years I've kept this light and I still trip on the third one.
Easy, easy. The tide spat you onto Driftwood Island, same as it did me forty years back. You're lucky to be breathing.
There's the one who silenced the Bell! Listen to that: nothing but gulls. Forty years I've waited for quiet like this.
Hah! The hero of Hollowgrave, on my doorstep. Kettle's on, you've earned the good tea.
Warden of the Horizon, they're calling you now. I always said you had the look of someone who'd go far. Well. I thought it.
Listen to that thunder. Nobody sane is at sea tonight.
Storm's right on top of us. Stay in the dry a while.
Every timber in the harbour's groaning. Ugly night.
Wretched rain. Gets into everything.
Rain again. Good for the cisterns, bad for the soul.
You're dripping on my floor, by the way.
Late to be wandering about.
Night's when the cursed come walking. Keep a lantern lit.
Can't sleep either, eh?
Up with the gulls, I see.
Early start, {player}.
Mist'll burn off by mid-morning.
Washed up here forty years back, same as you. My ship was the Margery Ann, out of Kingsport.
Everyone else aboard went down with her. I took the keeper's job because somebody had to keep the light, and because I couldn't bear to get on another ship.
Not once. I watch them come and go from the gallery. That's enough sea for me.
Once, in a fit of bravery, I rowed out to the reef. Got halfway and rowed back. Proudest day of my life.
Mind, now the Bell's quiet... maybe one day. A short trip. To Saltmarrow. With a lot of rum.
Driftwood's the gentlest island in the Reach: palms, a pier, the lighthouse and me. Wreckage washes up on the north beach after every storm.
Nothing much on Driftwood but sand, palms, the light and an old fool. The Old Chapel Crypt's under the hill if you want trouble, though.
Tomorrow morning the north beach will be covered in wreck. Get there before the gulls.
Out on Hollowgrave there's a bell under the water. When it tolls, the drowned get up and walk.
It's been tolling louder every year. Someone cast it to call the dead, and someone could cast another to silence it. That's what the stories say.
